### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 54 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `645cdbcb1c719457c9cdd3b7541d86196f76ef5e` — the merge of head `279ac14b605117de8e231ca8fdbd9e8287b022ab` into base `8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 645cdbcb1c719457c9cdd3b7541d86196f76ef5e && git checkout 645cdbcb1c719457c9cdd3b7541d86196f76ef5e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2 279ac14b605117de8e231ca8fdbd9e8287b022ab && git checkout -B drift-repro 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2 && git merge --no-ff 279ac14b605117de8e231ca8fdbd9e8287b022ab

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8f915f2a17c2f496c63a7b9d6b86b04aaf9a6ff2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `ead8d70a72e9dd9e6a7a6b00ab421ec7a3d9ad69`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration only. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial in the PR body and in `.changeset/33597-persona-grant-checks.md`, and supersedes the claim's `no` (card comment 6888520066). The file list has 6 files: the changeset, `docs/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `src/score/scenario-tags.ts`, `test/score/scenario-tags.test.ts` and `test/score/scenario-cards.test.ts`. None is under `packages/spec/src/**` or a governed path, and nothing declares a narrowing; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success on this head. I read the net diff against merge-base `6e287974`. The last commit `ead8d70a` over `0b8737ea` changes only the changeset's Clause-② line.

### ① Derived judgments

Published surface of `@objectstack/scenarios`, read against its `exports` map on main:

1. **New exports are additive and declared correctly.** `src/score/scenario-tags.ts` now exports `personaGrantNeeds`, `gradePersonaGrants`, `PersonaGrantVerb` and `PersonaGrantNeed`. `./score/full` reaches them (`src/score/index.ts` has `export *` from `scenario-tags.js`). The narrow `./score` entry does not reach them: tsup builds `score` from `src/score/narrow.ts`, which does not re-export `scenario-tags`.
2. **The `run` input type is widened correctly.** `ScenarioArtifactCard['run']` now also accepts optional `questions` and `operations` (a Partial Pick of the card schema's own type). Every earlier pick still type-checks.
3. **New output field: a widening for readers.** `ScenarioArtifactScore.personaGrants` is a required field on an output type. It also reaches `./runner` through the exported `BuildHalf.score` (`runner/index.ts` has `export *` from `orchestrate.js`), and the declaration does not name that (N1).
4. **Score behaviour change is real and declared.** `scoreScenarioArtifact` and `scoreCardArtifact` now count the persona-grant checks in `passed`, `total` and `score`, and leave out every check carrying `notMeasured`. On main, no expect, tag, agent-action or naming check sets `notMeasured`; only `scenario-operation-grade.ts` does, and it is outside this sum. So the exclusion moves only the new checks, and it makes real what `CheckResult.notMeasured` already documents in `scenario-score.ts`. The runner's build tally reads `score.passed` and `score.total`, so the CLI's Build cells and `degraded` move too. The declaration covers this ("a card's Build score can move").
5. **Imports add no new dependency.** The new imports are `buildEffectiveObjectPermissions` and `superuserFieldVote` from `@objectstack/core`, and `objectPermissionGrants` and `ObjectPermissionVerbTarget` from `@objectstack/spec/security`. `scenario-tags.ts` already depends on both packages. The narrow `./score` graph is unchanged and still reads core and spec only.
6. **Grading matches card done-when 1 as corrected by 6888060472.**
   - A question needs `read`. An `applied` or `pending_confirmation` operation needs its kind.
   - A `PERMISSION_DENIED` operation passes when the set grants no verb, or when an unconditioned entry on a field the write names is not editable. "Not editable" is `editable !== true`, the same reading core's `fieldPermissionVote` gives an unconditioned entry, and Modify All overrides the lock.
   - It is not measured when only an applying row policy or a row-conditioned field entry could refuse the write, and it fails otherwise.
   - When the same persona, object and verb is both needed and refused, only the needed check is produced, and its detail names the refusal.
   - Each set is looked up as namespace plus `_` plus persona id, through the existing `personaSetName`. That is the same `personaPermissionSetName` the runner's `permissionSetName` signs in with.
7. **Beyond the card's text:** a question asked as a persona that hides the object (`hidden.objects`) produces no read. This is right: a read would contradict the card's own hidden declaration, and the dev flagged it. The confirm-gated not-measured case on the needed arm is also beyond the card's text; see S1.
8. **Done-when 3 is met.** The tests pin a missing grant (the read-only contractor), a present grant, and a grant the card refuses: absent, granted, field lock, a lock on another field, Modify All override, and row rule only. The real `project_with_tasks` and `requisition_to_receipt` cards are used.

Gates: every check-run on this head concluded success or skipped, with none failed, cancelled or pending. This includes `Check Changeset` (2), `TypeScript Type Check`, the `Type Check` legs, `Test Core` (the aggregate plus 7 planned shards), `Build Core`, the `Lint` legs, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards`.

Findings:
- **S1 (should-fix, on the card; the head does not move).** The fork 2 (ii-a) case has no ruling on card #33597: a withheld write verb that only `pending_confirmation` operations need, with the build declaring the card's `confirm: true` agent action on that object, is not measured. Its only records are the dev report (6888503308) and the PR body's prose, while done-when 1 still reads "`pending_confirmation` ⇒ the verb on that object". On the merits it holds:
  - it is never a pass;
  - it matches the prompt's "Business actions an AI agent may call (… ask before acting where marked)";
  - tests pin that `confirm: false` is measured, that an applied delete is measured, and that the withheld update stays failed beside `set_task_status`.

  Fix: the seat records the ruling on the card, or edits done-when 1 the way 6888060472 did, before landing.
- **N1 (nit).** The declaration names `./score/full` alone. `personaGrants` and the moved totals also reach `./runner` through `BuildHalf.score`, and they reach the CLI's Build cells. The arm and the level do not change.
- **N2 (nit).** Card comment 6888520066 says `./score` re-exports `scenario-tags.ts`. It does not, because `narrow.ts` leaves it out. The PR body and the changeset state it correctly, and they govern.
- **N3 (nit).** `confirmGatedRoutes` matches only the card's `confirm: true` and the built action's name, not the built action's `ai.requiresConfirmation`. `gradeAgentActions` already fails that action separately, so the score still drops. Accepted.
- **N4 (nit, outside the diff).** The build evidence in the runner's `runRecord` (`src/runner/scorecard.ts`, near line 401) leaves out `personaGrants`. A failing grant check then degrades the build cell, but no clause names it. The dev flagged this. File it as a follow-up card, since the runner was off-limits here.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). This matches the diff: exports and an output field are added, and two input fields become optional. Nothing is removed, renamed or tightened, so it is not a narrowing, and no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is right. The scenario-card schema (`src/schema.ts`) is untouched, and nothing a metadata author can write changes.

`'@objectstack/scenarios': patch` is the right level. AGENTS.md says the level follows the protocol kind, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The package publishes, so `skip-changeset` does not apply. It is in the `fixed` group, and `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations and acceptance notes (6888503308 and the PR body):
- **Fork 2, first ruled (ii) and replaced by (ii-a):** the ruling is not on the card (S1).
- **Assignee and reviewer steps skipped by order:** this is process only and does not affect the contract.
- **#33596 `add_line` `unit_price` gap not visible:** out of scope; the sibling #33596 owns it. Answered.
- **Grants that do not trace to the prompt:** done-when 2's remedy is a card fix. The card names no card-fix cards, and `Fixes #33597` closes the card on merge. **Escalated to the seat:** file the card-fix cards and name them on #33597 before landing, or switch the PR to `Part-of`.
- **Questions asked as a persona that hides the object:** the derivation is right (① 7). Whether each card means "declines" is a card question.
- **isDefault, scratch versus template:** recorded as a gap not graded here in 6888060472. Answered.
- **Runner evidence-list follow-up:** N4.

Other items:
- **Claim correction 6888520066 (`no` to `yes (widening)`):** consistent with the diff. Answered.
- **`open_questions`:** the report carries none.
- **PR author:** `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `279ac14b605117de8e231ca8fdbd9e8287b022ab`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration only. This is the delta over record 6889624779, which reviewed head `ead8d70a`. The hop has two commits of the PR's own:
- `3d9c1695` merges `main` at `8f915f2a`;
- `279ac14b` changes three files: `src/runner/scorecard.ts` (+1 −1), `test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts` (+7) and the changeset (+2).

I compared each head against its own merge base: `ead8d70a` against `6e287974`, and `279ac14b` against `8f915f2a`. The changed lines of the six earlier files are identical in both, so the merge did not change the PR's net diff. The net diff now has 8 files, and the two new ones are exactly what `279ac14b` changes. None is under `packages/spec/src/**` or a governed path, and nothing declares a narrowing. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

The earlier findings:
- **S1: closed.** Card comment 6889635350 records the fork 2 (ii-a) ruling on #33597. It gives the carve-out from done-when 1 (a withheld write verb that only `pending_confirmation` operations need, where the card declares a `confirm: true` agent action and the build declares that action, is not measured and never a pass), the reason from the build prompt, and the controls that stay measured. This matches the code and tests I judged in 6889624779 ① 6 and ① 7, and the hop does not touch `scenario-tags.ts`.
- **N1: closed in the changeset, still open in the PR body.** The changeset now says that `personaGrants` reaches `./runner` through `BuildHalf.score`, and it names the run record's build evidence. The PR body's `Clause-②:` line still names `./score/full` alone (S2).
- **N2: closed.** Card comment 6889635350 corrects 6888520066: the narrow `./score` entry does not re-export `scenario-tags.ts`.
- **N3: accepted, unchanged.**
- **N4: closed in this PR, for the first build.** Commit `279ac14b` adds the build's persona grant checks to the `build` half's evidence in `runRecord`, between `agentActions` and `naming`. The new pin in `orchestrate.test.ts` runs the real crm card. It checks that the persona grant checks are not empty, and that the `persona-grant:` evidence on the `crm_account_with_contacts.scratch.build` result equals `personaGrants` in order. What is left is N5.

The hop's own change to the published surface:
1. **`./runner` output.** `runRecord` is exported from `./runner` (`runner/index.ts` has `export *` from `scorecard.js`). Each first-run build result now has one more `clauses` entry for each persona grant check. Its `verdict` still comes from the half's tally, which already counted these checks on `ead8d70a` (6889624779 ① 4), so no verdict, cell or `degraded` value moves. No type changes. This adds evidence for readers, and the changeset names it. Side effect: the `naming` clauses now come after the grant checks, so their `clause` indices shift (N6).
2. **The merged `main` and this PR fit together.** The merge brings in #33625 (sibling #33596) in the same package. It changes the same `scorecard.ts`, both READMEs and `orchestrate.test.ts`, and the PR's lines in them are unchanged. The two behave consistently. Under #33625, a write that the build denies the persona leaves the operation not measured, and it is listed as an unscored Build finding. Under this PR, the missing grant behind that denial fails a scored `persona-grant:` check in the Build half. The defect is charged to the build once and is not counted twice. #33625's own acceptance note names #33597 as where the Build half checks this.

Gates on this head: 48 check-runs. 19 are success and 16 skipped. None failed or was cancelled. **13 are still in progress:** `Test Core` shards 1/8 to 5/8, the three `Type Check` legs (workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates) and five `Lint` legs. The `Test Core` aggregate and `TypeScript Type Check` have not reported yet. Already success: `Check Changeset`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, and `Test Core` 6/8 and 7/8. The all-green check at landing is still owed on this head. The PR body's Verification section describes `0b8737ea` and `ead8d70a`, and records no local run of the new runner pin, so CI is the only evidence for `279ac14b`.

Findings:
- **S2 (should-fix, PR body only; the head does not move).** The PR body has not caught up with the seat's ruling or with this hop:
  - It still says `Fixes #33597`. Card comment 6889635350 rules that the PR "lands as `Part-of #33597`" and that the card stays open for the card-fix round of done-when 2. That is how the escalation in 6889624779 is resolved, but the body does not yet say so. If the PR merged as it stands, it would close the card that carries the card-fix round.
  - Four lines no longer match the diff:
    - the 维护者速读 line "不碰 runner";
    - the Files paragraph, which says `src/runner/**` is off-limits and not touched;
    - the "Follow-up, off-limits here" acceptance note, which this hop has done;
    - the body's `Clause-②:` line, which leaves out the `./runner` reach that the changeset now states (N1).

  Fix: switch the body to `Part-of #33597` and bring those four lines into line with the diff before landing. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` arm stays as it is.
- **N5 (nit, accepted, or a follow-up card).** The `iterate-build` evidence lists only `expect.checks` and `naming`. The iterate build is scored by `scoreCardArtifact` too (`orchestrate.ts` around line 555), so its tally also counts tags, agent actions and now persona grants, and none of these is named in its evidence. Tags and agent actions were already left out before this PR. This hop names the grant checks for the first build only.
- **N6 (nit, accepted).** In the run record's `build` result, the `clause` index of each `naming` check moves up by the number of persona grant checks. A reader that matches clauses across runs by index rather than by `evidence.check` would see them move. I found no reader on main that does: `scripts/qa/retest-owed.mjs` reads a checklist `QA-source:` clause, not a scenario run record's index.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). This still matches the diff. On top of the surface judged in 6889624779 ②, the hop adds evidence entries to an existing `./runner` output array. It changes no type and removes, renames or tightens nothing. It is not a narrowing, so no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

`Metadata-protocol: none` is still right: `src/schema.ts` and the card JSON are untouched.

`'@objectstack/scenarios': patch` is still the right level. The changeset's added paragraph keeps the same arm and level, and it now names both `./runner` reaches. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The PR now changes code its order kept off-limits.** The PR body records `src/runner/**` as off-limits by order, and `279ac14b` changes `src/runner/scorecard.ts`. Neither the card nor the PR records the seat lifting that limit. 6889624779 N4 asked for a follow-up card instead. On the merits the change is right, small and tested (① N4 and ① 1), and I accept it. The body refresh in S2 should say that the seat took N4 into this PR.
- **The escalation on card-fix cards:** the seat decided in 6889635350. The card stays open, and the seat dispatches the card fixes after this PR merges, checking the scope with eval#1 first. The PR side is still owed (S2).
- **The merge of `main`:** it did not change the PR's net diff (Face). The overlap with #33625 is judged in ① 2.
- **`open_questions`:** none were added after 6889624779.
- **PR author:** `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.
